metadata.direction: BIMCraft Rust is the primary development foundation. New BIMCraft Web development is frozen; preserve existing work for handoff.
metadata.newerObservedScope: Wireframe DirectX shader/edge changes, palette behavior and associated tests/translations. Observed, not runtime accepted or adopted.
metadata.evidencePolicy: Separate existing source capability, bounded release runtime evidence, reported upstream work and proposed acceptance. No entire Revit-parity claim.
metadata.publicationScope: Sanitized documentation only. No house models, images, local inventories, app code or maintainer messages.

tracks.title: Baseline and upstream workflow
tracks.benefit: Keep one reliable Rust baseline and small contributions that can return upstream.
tracks.current: Installed v0.10.0 is the comparison build. No SDH Rust feature branch or newer-main adoption is established by this audit.
tracks.next: Pin baseline, inventory existing commands and upstream overlap, register fixtures and designate one active implementation slice.
tracks.acceptance: Every run records codebase, exact commit, fixture hash and configuration. Vanilla, candidate and accepted builds remain distinct. Review upstream changes before each slice; never import an open PR as an accepted capability.

tracks.title: Mac interaction
tracks.benefit: Make daily navigation and editing comfortable on a Mac trackpad.
tracks.current: Release source maps scroll to zoom, pinch to zoom, middle drag to pan and primary drag/Shift-middle to orbit. Native Mac acceptance is incomplete.
tracks.next: Prototype a trackpad profile while preserving selection, Properties, numeric entry, cancellation and accessible command access.
tracks.acceptance: Proposed, not committed: two-finger pan, pinch zoom, modifier plus two-finger orbit. Test momentum, panel scrolling, context click, selection versus navigation, Retina scaling, gesture cancellation and OS-reserved gestures. Austin reviews intentional departures before dependent semantics are committed.

tracks.title: Revit and IFC import reliability
tracks.benefit: Open real residential exports with clear accounting for what survives.
tracks.current: Installed release rejects both original house exports at a 256 MiB guard. A compacted IFC4 copy opens with documented omissions. Newer source has roof changes; their effect on this house is untested.
tracks.next: Compare original IFC4 and IFC2X3 exports across pinned release and candidate; identify missing products by source identity; address large-file lifecycle and specific geometry/category failures.
tracks.acceptance: Preserve originals. Produce imported/transformed/skipped counts and identities, material/type/placement checks, geometry comparison and explicit unsupported cases. Large-file acceptance covers peak memory, cancellation, failure rollback, native save/reopen/autosave/recovery and linked files. Retain geometry-complexity bounds; no blanket removal of caps.

tracks.title: Model integrity and agent operations
tracks.benefit: Make manual and automated edits equally trustworthy.
tracks.current: Shared Session::execute, CLI and MCP exist. Release synthetic checks passed move/Undo/Redo, failed-operation rollback, hosted copy and native reopen. Document ownership and interleaving are not fully accepted.
tracks.next: Transfer precision/reference/history contracts; inventory actual MCP exposure and prove one reproducible local batch job.
tracks.acceptance: UI and semantic tools use the same operations. Verify stable identities, raw units, dirty/stale refusal, document binding, permission/revision checks, atomic failure, no-op receipts, owned Undo and preservation of human edits. Read-only calls do not mutate. Separate implemented, registered, transport-tested, packaged and connected evidence. Compare actual saved outputs independently.

tracks.title: Compound walls and joins
tracks.benefit: Produce predictable cores, finishes, corners and end conditions.
tracks.current: Automatic miters/node joins and six location references exist. Zero-thickness membrane layers are supported. Independent priority, explicit core boundaries, configurable per-end joins and wrapping parity are not established.
tracks.next: Start with documented/native reference cases and one layered 90-degree L corner; extend join choices, permissions, seams and free-end/insert wrapping as distinct slices.
tracks.acceptance: Compare core-butt/finish continuity, same/different materials, explicit butt/miter/order where eligible, physical permission versus view cleanup and untouched-end preservation after history. Verify plan/section/export/save/reopen and manual/MCP equivalence. Unsupported curves/heights fail or fall back explicitly.

tracks.title: Editing, hosting and building elements
tracks.benefit: Keep walls, openings, levels and residential elements coordinated as plans change.
tracks.current: Many Modify commands, hosts, levels and building elements already exist. Limited move/copy tests passed; complete lifecycle acceptance has not.
tracks.next: Audit existing commands before extending them; prove wall movement/copy with host rules, then opening lifecycle and level cascades.
tracks.acceptance: Test move/copy/rotate/mirror/align/offset/split, operation-specific snapping, grips/numeric input/Esc, type versus instance, flip, height/thickness changes, rehost/replace/delete, references, Undo and reopen. Inventory foundations/slabs/beams/stairs/railings/rooms individually; no implied engineering sizing or compliance.

tracks.title: Residential roofs
tracks.benefit: Handle the mixed pitches and intersections used in real homes.
tracks.current: Roof creation, joining and wall attachment exist. A simple gable passed a release smoke test. Newer source adds relevant per-edge slopes/import and shape-editing work; house fidelity remains unproved.
tracks.next: Use R02 findings to select a bounded correction, then prove pitch/bearing/overhangs, persistent intersections and attached-wall behavior.
tracks.acceptance: Fixtures include different pitches/bearings, porch and shed intersections, cross-gables, dormers and unequal overhangs. Verify stable references, edits, invalid-case diagnostics, eave/rake/fascia/soffit output, quantities, Undo, reopen and agent operations.

tracks.title: Families and reusable libraries
tracks.benefit: Build reusable residential components that remain editable.
tracks.current: Rust has parametric forms/formulas, hosted families and material/family favorites. The family editor is substantially text based. Imported IFC geometry does not recover the original RFA authoring graph.
tracks.next: Prove one parametric window in two sizes; define versioned material/assembly/component packages and safe updates. Graphical constrained editing follows later.
tracks.acceptance: Width/height/frame depth and host cuts must agree in model, drawings and quantities. Preserve type/instance distinction, overrides, identities, formulas and stable topology through edits/update/reopen. Package dependency/collision/version policy explicitly. Graphical sketch/history work needs recompute and failure recovery; do not begin with an engine rewrite.

tracks.title: Views and coordinated documentation
tracks.benefit: Turn the model into a consistent residential drawing set.
tracks.current: Plans, sections, elevations, dimensions, callouts and sheets exist. Dimension chains/constraints go beyond the initial Web slice. Family forms have sectioning limitations distinct from wall outlines.
tracks.next: Verify existing views and dimension workflows; build representative wall-base/window/eave details and one coordinated small-house set.
tracks.acceptance: Check plan/RCP view ranges, layers/detail levels, joined-wall and family sections, dimension witness references/locks/chains, callout associations, title blocks/scales/numbering/index and actual SVG/PDF output. Change the model and verify all affected drawings/schedules. Record intentional differences and unsupported commands honestly.

tracks.title: Schedules and quantity semantics
tracks.benefit: Make schedules and takeoffs mean what a builder expects.
tracks.current: Flexible schedules, filters/grouping/calculations and CSV/XLSX exist in inspected source. Exact Web assembly-layer legend semantics are not established; room volume is not roof/ceiling-clipped equivalence.
tracks.next: Transfer layer-order/core/cavity/membrane definitions and hand-checkable gross/net material cases.
tracks.acceptance: Independently reconcile known areas/volumes/counts, opening deductions, finish coverage, cavity non-solid volume, zero-thickness membranes and framing member quantities. Verify unit rounding, updates, exports and read-only semantic calls; a flexible table is not proof of correct quantities.

tracks.title: Framing and assembly coordination
tracks.benefit: Reveal framing and coordinate outlets and shower niches within real stud bays.
tracks.current: No equivalent complete automatic timber-wall/stud-bay workflow was established in Rust. Structural beams or rebar do not demonstrate this capability. Web framing proof is reference evidence.
tracks.next: One straight timber wall, one rectangular opening, one outlet and one niche; richer assembly transitions and junctions follow later.
tracks.acceptance: One authoritative wall drives finished/core/framing views. Deterministic members and bay identities survive supported edits; placements retain stud-side/bay intent or report conflict. Preserve overrides and kept pieces. Niche clear width/height/depth and allowances remain distinct; no silent stud deletion or treating every niche as a through opening.

tracks.title: Performance, recovery and delivery
tracks.benefit: Keep the real house responsive and upgrades dependable.
tracks.current: Native desktop packaging exists. Synthetic smoke evidence is not a house-scale performance baseline. Existing Web performance collection remains evidence, not native acceptance.
tracks.next: Measure Mac CPU/GPU/memory/import/edit/view/export performance; fix measured bottlenecks. Add large-project recovery, migration, locale and packaging acceptance.
tracks.acceptance: Use repeatable real-house and synthetic fixtures with hardware/configuration and percentile reporting. Prior 100 ms selection / 33 ms preview / 500 ms committed-edit p95 goals are proposed, not achieved. Verify upgrades, old/new format handling, autosave/recovery, offline use, localized text and export fonts. No Web-to-Rust/WASM rewrite spike remains.

tracks.title: Capture to parametric BIM
tracks.benefit: Reconstruct editable models from measured reference evidence.
tracks.current: Retained goal; no complete capture-to-authoritative-BIM workflow accepted.
tracks.next: Keep deferred until the residential foundation is trustworthy.
tracks.acceptance: Separate uncertain scan/reference evidence from confirmed dimensions. Require measurement confirmation and semantic, editable reconstruction with coordinated drawings; capture uncertainty must not weaken model precision.

firstSlices.title: Pin the baseline and preserve comparison builds
firstSlices.acceptance: Exact commits, fixture hashes, hardware/build configuration and source/runtime evidence ledger; one active implementation slice, owner and isolated checkout recorded.

firstSlices.title: Compare house imports and explain every omission
firstSlices.acceptance: Both original exports, release/candidate results, source-product identities and reasons for omissions; compare missing roof geometry and materials without changing masters. Record memory/time and original-file refusal.

firstSlices.title: Prototype native Mac trackpad navigation
firstSlices.acceptance: Review proposed mapping before committing dependent semantics. Verify pan/zoom/orbit, selection, panel scroll, cancellation, context click and momentum on the actual Mac.

firstSlices.title: Prove model/history ownership and agent parity
firstSlices.acceptance: Manual/core/real MCP edits agree; stale/dirty/wrong-document interleaving cannot modify or Undo unrelated work; independent saved-file checks, rollback and receipts.

firstSlices.title: Fix the smallest verified import failure
firstSlices.acceptance: Choose the defect from measured comparison, provide a synthetic reproducer and upstream-compatible correction, then rerun affected house and unsupported controls.

firstSlices.title: Large-file import and persistence lifecycle
firstSlices.acceptance: Document an explicit resource policy instead of merely deleting MAX_FILE. Exercise below/at/above thresholds, original files, native save/open, autosave/recovery and links, peak memory, UI responsiveness, cancellation and failure rollback. Exact 256 MiB is currently refused.

sharedAcceptance: Record Revit reference versions and distinguish documentation, native observation and inference.
Define activation, selection, context, Properties/type distinction, grips, numeric input, snapping, hosts/layers, Esc, Undo/Redo, save/reopen and output as applicable.
Present material semantic ambiguity or intentional departures before committing dependent behavior.
Manual and semantic operations share authoritative model validation/history; verify actual client transport and independently inspect saved outputs.
Preserve fixture masters and owner checkouts. No giant parallel feature rollout. One active implementation slice and small upstream-compatible contributions.
An upstream PR, source feature, smoke test and accepted product workflow are different evidence levels.
